# The tests that do not open with t.Parallel(), one `path:TestName serial: <reason>`
# per line (internal/ci/parallel_class_test.go, Glenn 2026-09-25: Go tests always
# run in parallel). The reasons are what makes a test unsafe beside another:
#   t.Setenv, t.Chdir     panic under t.Parallel (the testing package refuses both)
#   os.Setenv, os.Chdir   change the whole process under every other test
#   swaps package var X   the test (or a helper it calls) assigns a package-level
#                         seam, which races every parallel test reading it
# The way off this list is a per-test seam: cmd.Env for a child, a field on the
# value under test for a clock or a dialer, t.TempDir for a path. The list only
# shrinks: a test that opens with t.Parallel() while listed, or a listed test
# that is gone, is a red run, and the ceiling line below caps the count.
#
# The ceiling is the row count; it only comes down. NOVA_CI_UPDATE=1 drops the
# stale rows and lowers it in the same write, and never raises it (#4339).
# History: 877 on the day the rule landed; 2026-09-25 evening it rose by nine for
# tests the fleet, redis, nova-sprint and swarm streams landed after the
# measurement with t.Setenv or a package-var seam (card_moves TestCardSessionCLI
# and TestCardMovesCLI, fleet_build TestFleetBuildCompileVerb and
# ...ExecGivesGoItsOwnCaches, jev TestJevMechRefusals, lander_unit
# TestLanderLoadsMembersFromUnitRecords, line TestLineVerbPostListImport,
# task_card TestTaskMoveRefusesAPrimaryUnread, card
# TestReadCopyDealtToBenchRendersALintedCard), then by nine more from the redis
# stream (seat and #3277 tests on t.Setenv); each owes a per-test seam. Moved
# from the serialTestsCeiling constant into this file at 876, the count that day.
# ceiling: 565
